strategy.summary: Reproduce pandas issue #54380 / PR #63143 (rolling skew/kurt numerical instability, roll_kurt in aggregations.pyx) by building the buggy commit eaabb41d17ca with its Cython extension, then running the rolling tests added by the PR. The defect should appear as wrong or polluted kurt values on large-magnitude data, and the PR's tests should fail there and pass on the fixed revision after a rebuild.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang) for building the Cython extension
pinned_because: No version pins: NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata and Cython have documented_constraint null and era_ceiling null, so no bound is applied. NumPy 2.4.6 and bottleneck 1.6.0 come from the issue#69037 environment listing and are undocumented, so they are a sample rather than a requirement. Build tooling (meson-python, meson, ninja, pytest) is not in the evidence and is included only so the editable build can run.

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest pandas/tests/window/test_rolling.py -k 'same_result_with_different_lengths or rolling_skew_kurt_large_value_range or rolling_skew_kurt_numerical_stability' -q
strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/window/test_rolling.py::test_same_result_with_different_lengths (parametrized over method in skew, kurt), plus the new kurt case in test_rolling_skew_kurt_large_value_range with data [1e6, -1e6, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], window 4, and expected [nan, nan, nan, 1.5, 4.0, -1.2, -1.2, -1.2]
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy eaabb41d17ca (extension rebuilt from that revision), at least one of the selected tests fails: test_same_result_with_different_lengths[kurt] compares a 10-element rolling result against the first 10 rows of a 12-element rolling result with check_exact=True and mismatches, and/or the new large_value_range kurt case mismatches its expected values. On the fixed revision (extension rebuilt from the PR commit), all selected tests pass.
strategy.numerical_probe: Run Series(rng.normal(loc=0.0, scale=1e3, size=12)) with rolling(8).kurt() on the first 10 and all 12 values with np.random.default_rng(2), and compare the overlapping prefix exactly.
risks: Transition requires a rebuild of the Cython extension between revisions; running the tests with a stale build from the other revision will give a false result.

The reporter and maintainer disagreed on whether precision loss is the cause; the new tests use magnitudes of 1e3 and 1e6, so the buggy failure should appear there, but the moderate-magnitude regime is not established by the evidence.

The length-consistency test uses check_exact=True, so it depends on the exact floating-point operation order. Results may differ across CPU architecture, compiler, optimisation flags, or SIMD, so the transition may not reproduce on ARM, macOS, or a different compiler. Those platforms are not assumed by the evidence.
Dtype and precision are not stated in the evidence; the test data is float64 because of the 1e6 floats in the list, but this is inferred.
Expected values for the GH 61416 case are given in the test diff but the buggy output is not recorded, so the exact failing values are unknown.
The default assert_series_equal tolerance used by the parametrized large_value_range case is not stated in the evidence.
Bottleneck is in the environment listing but is not on the rolling kurt path; it is kept installed only to match the reported environment.
Python version is not stated in the evidence; the build should use whatever version the repository's supported range allows.

oracle.tolerance: large_value_range uses assert_series_equal default (value not stated in evidence); length test uses exact comparison (check_exact=True)
oracle.reference_source: test diff in PR #63143 (tests in pandas/tests/window/test_rolling.py)
oracle.why: Two checks are used: a tolerance-based comparison for the large-value-range kurt case and an exact comparison of skew/kurt across different series lengths.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision, the exact prefix comparison in test_same_result_with_different_lengths[kurt] (and possibly the new kurt case in large_value_range) should see different values for the same window, because the running fourth-moment update carries error from earlier values into later windows, so the assertion fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision, roll_kurt recomputes from scratch on instability and uses the online central-moment update, so the shorter and longer series give identical windows and the expected values match, and the assertions pass.
